milestones.title: Three weeks of mornings held
milestones.criteria: Twelve morning sessions done, every set stopped at the last clean rep, and the log has a number for every one.

milestones.title: Sets of 8-10 clean reps
milestones.criteria: You're finishing six sets of 8-10 clean reps in a session — more reps per set than your starting max, repeated six times.

milestones.title: First max test logged
milestones.criteria: The week 7 Saturday test is done and filmed, and the number is written down — whatever it is.

milestones.title: 30 unbroken push-ups
milestones.criteria: One filmed or watched all-out set of 30 clean push-ups, stopping only when form would have broken.

protocol.coach_notes: The whole plan rests on one idea: your 8 dies on form, so every set you do stops one rep before that happens. That's not caution, it's the thing that makes 30 possible — sloppy reps build nothing and cost you shoulders. If you miss a morning, do it the next morning and carry on; one missed day is noise, two in a row is where plans go to die. And when week 7's test comes back lower than you hoped, don't panic and add extra sessions — the taper in week 8 is what puts the real number on the board.

sessions.goal: Hold a basic 5-minute conversation in Spanish within 3 month

protocol.goal_statement: Hold a basic 5-minute conversation in Spanish in 12 weeks, starting from ~20 words, using 30 minutes each morning plus your partner as a live practice partner.
protocol.short_title: Hold a 5-minute Spanish conversation in 12 weeks

phases.title: The 30 minutes that always happen
phases.focus: Get the morning block running every day it's scheduled and start saying real sentences out loud from day one — even bad ones.

steps.title: Do the 30-minute morning Spanish block
steps.details: Same slot every weekday and Saturday morning, before work, before anything else. Coffee made the night before, phone on the kitchen counter, notebook open to yesterday's page. Split it: 10 minutes reviewing yesterday's words out loud, 15 minutes on today's new material, 5 minutes saying full sentences to yourself.

how_to.gist: 30 minutes in the same morning slot, six days a week — review, new material, then talk.
how_to.why: Thirty minutes a day is the whole engine of this plan. Six mornings a week for twelve weeks is what turns twenty words into a five-minute conversation.

sections.heading: The slot
sections.body: Before work, before your phone, before anything else. The night before, set out your notebook and pen and make the coffee. You are not deciding whether to do this in the morning — the decision was made tonight.

sections.heading: The 30 minutes
items: 10 min — say yesterday's words and phrases out loud, from memory first, then check
15 min — today's new material: listen, repeat aloud, write the phrases by hand
5 min — talk to yourself in full sentences using everything you know so far

sections.heading: The rule
sections.body: Out loud, always. Reading silently builds recognition, not speech, and speech is the thing you're chasing. If you can only manage 15 minutes some mornings, do 15 minutes out loud rather than 30 minutes silent.

sections.heading: If you slip
sections.body: Missing one morning is noise. Missing two in a row is how this dies. If you miss a morning, the next morning happens no matter what, even if it's only ten minutes.

how_to.counts_as_done: 30 minutes done out loud in the morning slot — six mornings this week, any order.

steps.week_progression: Weeks 1-3: the goal is showing up, not volume. If a morning runs short, cut the new material, never the out-loud review.

steps.title: Learn 8 new words or phrases and use each one out loud
steps.details: Eight is deliberately small. Pick phrases you'd actually say — greetings, ordering, asking where something is, saying you don't understand. Write each one by hand, say it aloud five times, then use it in a sentence about your own day. Yesterday's eight get said out loud again before you add today's.

how_to.gist: Eight new phrases a morning, written by hand and said aloud in a sentence about your own life.
how_to.why: You start with about twenty words. Eight a morning is small enough to actually stick and adds up to roughly 250 phrases by the end — more than enough for five minutes of basics.

sections.heading: Pick them
sections.body: Choose phrases you would genuinely say this week: greeting someone, ordering food, asking a price, saying you don't understand, asking someone to repeat. Skip anything you can't picture yourself using.

sections.heading: Learn them
items: Write the phrase by hand once
Say it aloud five times
Make one sentence of your own with it
Say yesterday's eight aloud before adding today's

sections.heading: The rule
sections.body: A phrase you can read is not a phrase you know. If you can't say it without looking, it goes on tomorrow's list again.

sections.heading: If it feels slow
sections.body: It will. Weeks 1-3 feel like nothing is landing — that's normal at this stage and it's not a sign the plan isn't working.

how_to.counts_as_done: Eight new phrases written, said aloud, and used in a sentence of your own.

steps.week_progression: Weeks 1-3: eight a morning. If you're keeping up easily, keep it at eight — the review matters more than the count right now.

steps.title: Sunday conversation with your partner
steps.details: Fifteen minutes, Sunday, with your partner — in Spanish the whole way through, however badly it goes. No correcting mid-sentence; they let you finish, then tell you the one or two things worth fixing. Bring the week's phrases and try to use them. English only if you're truly stuck, and then back to Spanish.

how_to.gist: Fifteen minutes of Spanish-only talk with your partner every Sunday, mistakes and all.
how_to.why: You have a live Spanish speaker at home — that's the single biggest advantage a beginner can have, and it's the exact skill you're chasing. Talking to a person beats tapping an app every time.

sections.heading: The setup
sections.body: Same time each Sunday, fifteen minutes, phones face down. You talk, they listen. It's a conversation, not a lesson.

sections.heading: The rules
items: Spanish the whole way through, even when it's clumsy
They don't correct you mid-sentence — let you finish first
Afterwards they name one or two things to fix, no more
English only if you're truly stuck, then straight back to Spanish

sections.heading: What to talk about
sections.body: Your day, the week ahead, what you ate, where you want to go. Bring the phrases you learned this week and force them into the conversation.

sections.heading: If it goes badly
sections.body: It will, for the first month. Fifteen clumsy minutes is the point — that's the rep. The conversation getting smoother is the whole goal.

how_to.counts_as_done: Fifteen minutes of Spanish-only conversation with your partner happened.

steps.week_progression: Weeks 1-3: fifteen minutes, mostly you struggling. That's correct. Don't extend it until it stops feeling like a cliff.

steps.title: Say the week's phrases out loud from memory
steps.details: Before you learn anything new each morning, close the notebook and say last week's phrases from memory, out loud. Whatever you can't produce, mark it and put it back in rotation. This is the five minutes that stops the early weeks from evaporating.

how_to.gist: Notebook closed — say last week's phrases from memory, out loud, before anything new.
how_to.why: New phrases pile up fast and old ones vanish just as fast. This is the five minutes that makes what you learned last week still be there next month.

sections.heading: How
sections.body: Notebook closed, no peeking. Say them out loud, one after another. When you stall, note the phrase and move on — don't sit there grinding on it.

sections.heading: What to do with the gaps
sections.body: Anything you couldn't produce goes back into today's list. Anything you produced easily can drop out of rotation for a few days.

sections.heading: Why it's separate
sections.body: Recognising a phrase when you see it and producing it from nothing are different skills. Only one of them works in a conversation.

how_to.counts_as_done: Last week's phrases said out loud from memory, notebook closed.

steps.week_progression: Weeks 1-3: cover the whole week's phrases. From week 4 this step grows to cover everything learned so far.

phases.title: Building sentences that hold together
phases.focus: Move from single phrases to connected sentences, and start steering the Sunday conversation instead of surviving it.

steps.title: Do the 30-minute morning Spanish block
steps.details: Same slot, same 30 minutes, but the split shifts: 10 minutes reviewing everything learned so far out loud, 10 minutes of new material, 10 minutes speaking — describing your day, your plans, what you want, in full sentences.

how_to.gist: Same 30-minute morning block, but a third of it is now you talking in full sentences.
how_to.why: You've got phrases. Now they need to connect. The extra speaking time is what turns a pile of words into something you can actually hold a conversation with.

sections.heading: The new split
items: 10 min — everything learned so far, said out loud from memory
10 min — new material: verbs, connecting words, question forms
10 min — talking: describe your day, your plans, ask yourself questions and answer them

sections.heading: The talking part
sections.body: This is the uncomfortable ten minutes and the most valuable one. Talk to yourself out loud about what you're actually doing that day. When you hit a word you don't have, write it down and look it up after — don't stop the sentence.

sections.heading: The rule
sections.body: Full sentences, not single words. 'Quiero café' becomes 'Quiero un café porque tengo sueño.' Length is the point.

how_to.counts_as_done: 30 minutes done, including ten minutes of talking in full sentences.

steps.week_progression: Weeks 4-7: the speaking ten minutes grows from describing your day to describing your plans and asking questions.

steps.title: Learn 10 new phrases and 5 verbs a morning
steps.details: Ten phrases plus five verbs you'll actually use — want, need, have, go, can. Learn each verb in the forms you'll say most: I, you, we. Write them by hand, say them aloud, then build three sentences with each verb about your own life.

how_to.gist: Ten new phrases and five everyday verbs a morning, each verb used in three sentences about you.
how_to.why: Verbs are what let you say things instead of naming things. Five a morning, always in the forms you'll actually say, is what gets you from pointing at objects to holding a conversation.

sections.heading: The verbs
sections.body: Start with the ones you'd use fifty times a day: want, need, have, go, can. Learn them as 'I want', 'you want', 'we want' — not as a grammar table.

sections.heading: The drill
items: Write the verb forms by hand
Say each aloud five times
Build three sentences with it about your own day
Say yesterday's verbs aloud before adding today's

sections.heading: The rule
sections.body: Every new verb gets used in a sentence about your actual life. 'Quiero ir al trabajo' sticks; a conjugation table doesn't.

how_to.counts_as_done: Ten phrases and five verbs learned, each verb used in three sentences of your own.

steps.week_progression: Weeks 4-7: five verbs a morning. By week 7 you should have the everyday ones covered and be adding past-tense forms.

steps.title: Sunday conversation with your partner
steps.details: Twenty-five minutes now, and you lead it. You pick the topic before you sit down and you ask the questions. Your partner answers in Spanish and asks you back. Still no correcting mid-sentence — notes afterwards, one or two things.

how_to.gist: Twenty-five minutes of Spanish with your partner, and this time you're the one asking the questions.
how_to.why: Fifteen minutes of surviving is done. Leading the conversation — picking the topic, asking — is the skill the five-minute target actually tests.

sections.heading: Before you sit down
sections.body: Pick the topic yourself: the weekend, food, work, a trip you want to take. Write three questions you'll ask. That's your job for the first five minutes.

sections.heading: The rules
items: You lead — you ask, they answer, they ask back
Spanish throughout, no mid-sentence corrections
They give you one or two fixes at the end
If you stall, ask for the word in Spanish before switching to English

sections.heading: If you run dry
sections.body: Have your week's phrases written on a card in front of you. Glancing at it is fine. Going silent for a minute is fine too — say so in Spanish and keep going.

how_to.counts_as_done: Twenty-five minutes of Spanish conversation, with you asking the questions.

steps.week_progression: Weeks 4-7: 25 minutes, you leading. If it's going well, add five minutes rather than adding a second session.

steps.title: Say everything learned so far out loud from memory
steps.details: Notebook closed. Work back through everything — phrases, verbs, sentence patterns — saying each aloud from memory. Anything that won't come gets marked and recycled into the day's new material. This is the step that keeps month one's work alive in month three.

how_to.gist: Notebook closed — work back through everything learned so far, out loud, from memory.
how_to.why: By week 4 the pile is big enough that old material starts sliding away. Revisiting it out loud is the difference between learning Spanish and just being exposed to it.

sections.heading: How
sections.body: Notebook closed. Go back through the phrases and verbs in order, saying each aloud. When one won't come, mark it and move on — don't stop the run.

sections.heading: The gaps
sections.body: Anything marked goes into today's new material. Anything that came easily can rest for a few days.

sections.heading: The point
sections.body: Producing from nothing is the skill that shows up in a conversation. Recognising it on a page is not.

how_to.counts_as_done: Everything learned so far said out loud from memory, notebook closed.

steps.week_progression: Weeks 4-7: the whole backlog, every morning. It takes longer each week — that's the step working.

phases.title: Holding a conversation, not surviving one
phases.focus: Push the Sunday conversation past five minutes and get comfortable being asked things you didn't prepare for.

steps.title: Do the 30-minute morning Spanish block
steps.details: Same slot. Now: 10 minutes reviewing everything out loud, 5 minutes of new material, 15 minutes of speaking — half of it rehearsing the questions your partner actually asks you, half of it talking about something you haven't prepared.

how_to.gist: Same morning block, now half of it is speaking — including things you haven't rehearsed.
how_to.why: A real conversation includes questions you didn't see coming. Practising the unprepared part in the morning is what stops the Sunday conversation from falling apart the moment it goes off script.

sections.heading: The split
items: 10 min — everything learned so far, out loud from memory
5 min — new material, less of it now
15 min — speaking: rehearse likely questions, then talk about something unprepared

sections.heading: The unprepared half
sections.body: Pick a random topic — what's in the fridge, a film you saw, your commute — and talk about it for two minutes without planning. Clumsy is fine. Stopping is the thing to avoid.

sections.heading: The rule
sections.body: When you don't have the word, talk around it in Spanish. Describing the thing you can't name is a real conversational skill and it's the one that saves you on the day.

how_to.counts_as_done: 30 minutes done, including fifteen minutes of speaking, half of it unprepared.

steps.week_progression: Weeks 8-10: new material drops to five minutes; speaking grows to fifteen.

steps.title: Sunday conversation with your partner
steps.details: Thirty-five minutes, and the last ten are unscripted — no topic picked in advance, no prepared questions. Your partner leads that stretch and asks whatever they like. You stay in Spanish and talk your way around anything you can't say directly.

how_to.gist: Thirty-five minutes with your partner, and the last ten are completely unscripted.
how_to.why: Five minutes of basic conversation means handling whatever comes at you, not reciting a prepared script. The unscripted stretch is where that gets built.

sections.heading: The shape
items: First 25 min — you lead, topic of your choosing
Last 10 min — no topic, no prep, your partner leads
Corrections only at the very end, one or two things

sections.heading: When you get stuck
sections.body: Describe around it in Spanish — 'the thing you use to open the door' works fine. Switching to English is the last resort, and you go straight back.

sections.heading: The target
sections.body: By week 10 you should be able to hold the whole thing in Spanish without a rescue. If you're not there yet, that's information, not failure — it just means the next two weeks are about this.

how_to.counts_as_done: Thirty-five minutes of Spanish, including ten minutes with no preparation at all.

steps.week_progression: Weeks 8-10: 35 minutes, last ten unscripted. This is the closest thing to the real target you'll do before week 12.

steps.title: Learn 10 new phrases a morning
steps.details: Ten a morning, but now they're the phrases that fill gaps you've actually hit — the things you wanted to say on Sunday and couldn't. Write them by hand, say them aloud, use each in a sentence about your own life.

how_to.gist: Ten phrases a morning, chosen from the things you actually wanted to say and couldn't.
how_to.why: By now your gaps are specific, not general. Learning the exact phrases you reached for and missed is the fastest possible progress from here.

sections.heading: Where they come from
sections.body: Keep a running list during the week of everything you wanted to say and couldn't. That list is your material — not a textbook's order.

sections.heading: The drill
items: Write each phrase by hand
Say it aloud five times
Use it in a sentence about your own life
Say yesterday's ten aloud before adding today's

sections.heading: The rule
sections.body: If a phrase has been on the list for three days and still won't stick, it's too long. Break it into a shorter version you can actually say.

how_to.counts_as_done: Ten phrases learned, written by hand and used in a sentence of your own.

steps.week_progression: Weeks 8-10: ten a morning, drawn from your own gap list rather than a fixed course.

steps.title: Say everything learned so far out loud from memory
steps.details: Notebook closed, everything from all ten weeks said aloud from memory. This now takes most of the review slot and that's correct — it's the step that makes the difference between knowing a lot of words and being able to reach for them mid-sentence.

how_to.gist: Notebook closed — everything from all ten weeks, out loud, from memory.
how_to.why: Reaching for a word mid-sentence is the exact skill the five-minute target tests. This is where that gets built.

sections.heading: How
sections.body: Notebook closed. Work back through everything, out loud. Mark what won't come and move on rather than grinding.

sections.heading: The gaps
sections.body: Marked phrases go into today's material. Anything that came easily can rest.

sections.heading: If it takes the whole slot
sections.body: Then it takes the whole slot. Reviewing what you know beats adding more you'll forget.

how_to.counts_as_done: Everything learned so far said out loud from memory, notebook closed.

steps.week_progression: Weeks 8-10: the full backlog every morning, gaps recycled into the day's new phrases.

phases.title: Five minutes, for real
phases.focus: Run the actual target conversation repeatedly until five minutes of Spanish is ordinary rather than an event.

steps.title: Do the 30-minute morning Spanish block
steps.details: Same slot, and now almost all of it is speaking: 10 minutes reviewing out loud, 20 minutes talking — including at least one full five-minute stretch where you don't stop, don't switch to English, and talk your way around anything you're missing.
steps.week_progression: Weeks 11-12: the unbroken stretch is the whole point of the phase. If five minutes is easy, go to six.

steps.title: Sunday conversation with your partner
steps.details: Forty minutes, and the middle five are the target: five minutes straight, Spanish only, no English rescue, no notes. Your partner keeps it going and doesn't let you off the hook. The rest of the session is normal conversation around it.

how_to.gist: Forty minutes with your partner, including five straight minutes of Spanish-only, no rescue.
how_to.why: This is the goal itself, rehearsed. Five minutes with no English and no notes is exactly what you set out to do — doing it twice before week 12 makes it ordinary.

sections.heading: The five minutes
sections.body: Pick a topic, set a timer, go. Spanish only. No notes, no English, no pausing to look anything up. Your partner keeps the conversation moving and doesn't bail you out.

sections.heading: Around it
sections.body: The other thirty-five minutes are normal conversation — warm up for ten, debrief for twenty-five afterwards, corrections at the end.

sections.heading: If you don't make five
sections.body: Note where it broke down and bring those exact gaps into Monday morning. Then do it again next Sunday. Two attempts is usually enough.

how_to.counts_as_done: Five unbroken minutes of Spanish-only conversation with your partner, plus the rest of the session.

steps.week_progression: Weeks 11-12: five minutes unbroken in week 11, and in week 12 do it twice in the same session.

steps.title: Learn 10 new phrases a morning
steps.details: Ten a morning, still drawn from the gaps you hit while speaking. Write, say aloud, use in a sentence. These are the phrases that make the next five-minute run smoother than the last one.

how_to.gist: Ten phrases a morning, taken straight from the gaps that broke your last five-minute run.
how_to.why: Every phrase you learn now closes a specific hole that showed up in real speech. That's the fastest route to a smoother five minutes.

sections.heading: Where they come from
sections.body: Straight from the five-minute run and the Sunday conversation — the exact things you reached for and didn't have.

sections.heading: The drill
items: Write each phrase by hand
Say it aloud five times
Use it in a sentence about your own life
Say yesterday's ten aloud before adding today's

sections.heading: The rule
sections.body: Short beats complete. A phrase you can say under pressure is worth more than a perfect one you fumble.

how_to.counts_as_done: Ten phrases learned, written by hand and used in a sentence of your own.

steps.week_progression: Weeks 11-12: ten a morning, all gap-filling. Nothing new for its own sake.

steps.title: Say everything learned so far out loud from memory
steps.details: Notebook closed, the full twelve weeks said aloud from memory. This is the last thing you do before the five-minute run each morning — it's what makes the words available when you need them mid-sentence.

how_to.gist: Notebook closed — the full twelve weeks, out loud, from memory, before the five-minute run.
how_to.why: Words you can produce from nothing are the ones that show up when you're mid-sentence and can't stop to think. This is the last rehearsal before the real thing.

sections.heading: How
sections.body: Notebook closed, everything out loud. Mark what won't come and move on.

sections.heading: The gaps
sections.body: Marked phrases go into today's ten. Anything easy can rest.

sections.heading: Then
sections.body: Straight into the five-minute run while everything is fresh and available.

how_to.counts_as_done: Everything learned across twelve weeks said out loud from memory, notebook closed.

steps.week_progression: Weeks 11-12: the full backlog, then straight into the unbroken five minutes.

milestones.title: Three weeks of mornings, unbroken
milestones.criteria: You did the 30-minute morning block at least 15 of the 18 scheduled mornings, and you've had three Sunday conversations with your partner.

milestones.title: You led the conversation
milestones.criteria: You picked the topic, asked the questions, and held 25 minutes of Spanish with your partner without switching to English more than a couple of times.

milestones.title: Ten unscripted minutes
milestones.criteria: You held ten minutes of Spanish on a topic nobody prepared, and talked your way around the words you didn't have.

milestones.title: Five minutes, no rescue
milestones.criteria: Five straight minutes of Spanish conversation with your partner — no English, no notes, no stopping.

protocol.coach_notes: Weeks 1-3 are going to feel like nothing is landing. That's not the plan failing — that's what starting from twenty words feels like, and it's the exact stretch where most people quit. Keep showing up and the payoff arrives late and all at once. One missed morning is noise; the morning after a miss is the one that decides this, so never miss two in a row. And lean on your partner — a live speaker at home is worth more than any app you could download.

protocol.goal_statement: Walk 10,000 steps a day consistently, built from a 4,000-step baseline via a lunch walk and an after-work walk.
protocol.short_title: Walk 10,000 steps a day in 10 weeks

phases.title: Two walks, every workday
phases.focus: Get the lunch walk and the after-work walk to happen on all five workdays, and start counting what you actually walk.

steps.title: Lunch walk
steps.details: Out the door within five minutes of finishing lunch, 20 minutes at a normal walking pace. Same route every day so you don't have to decide anything. Shoes stay under your desk.

how_to.gist: 20 minutes out the door within five minutes of finishing lunch
how_to.why: Your lunch break is the one window in a desk day nobody else can claim. This walk is the single biggest chunk of the 6,000 steps you're adding, and it only works if it starts before the afternoon can swallow it.

sections.heading: The window
sections.body: The moment you finish eating, you stand up and go. Not after one more email, not after you check one thing. Five minutes is the whole grace period — past that, the afternoon wins.

sections.heading: The route
sections.body: Pick one loop and walk the same one every day. A fixed route means no deciding, no checking your phone for directions, no reason to bail. If it's raining, walk it anyway or do laps inside the building.

sections.heading: Set it up
items: Walking shoes under your desk, not at home
A jacket or umbrella kept at work
Phone charged, headphones in your bag
Calendar blocked 12:30-1:00 as 'out'

how_to.counts_as_done: 20 minutes of walking, started within five minutes of finishing lunch.

steps.week_progression: Weeks 1-3: 20 minutes, same route, same time every day.

steps.title: After-work walk
steps.details: 20 minutes as soon as you get home — before you sit down, before you change out of work clothes. Walk out and back from your front door. If you get home late, do 10 minutes rather than skipping it.

how_to.gist: 20 minutes the moment you get home, before you sit down
how_to.why: The couch is undefeated once you're in it. This walk happens in the gap between the front door and the sofa, which is the only place it survives.

sections.heading: The rule
sections.body: Keys down, shoes on, out the door. You are not sitting down first. Sitting down is the whole risk — once you're down, the walk is gone.

sections.heading: The route
sections.body: Out your front door and back, 10 minutes each way. Nothing to plan, nothing to drive to. Same direction every day.

sections.heading: Late days
sections.body: If you get home after 8pm, do 10 minutes instead of 20. A short walk keeps the day alive; a skipped one starts the slide.

how_to.counts_as_done: 20 minutes of walking (10 on a late night), done before you sat down.

steps.week_progression: Weeks 1-3: 20 minutes, immediately on arriving home.

steps.title: Saturday long walk
steps.details: One 40-minute walk on Saturday, somewhere you actually like walking. This is the day that makes up ground when the workweek goes sideways.

how_to.gist: One 40-minute walk on Saturday, somewhere you like
how_to.why: Five workdays of walking leaves no room for error. Saturday is your cushion — it's where the week's total gets topped up when a meeting ate Tuesday.

sections.heading: Where
sections.body: Pick a place you'd walk anyway — a park, a waterfront, a neighborhood you like. This is the one walk of the week that's supposed to be pleasant, so don't make it a parking lot loop.

sections.heading: When
sections.body: Morning is easier than evening. Get it done before the day fills up and the rest of Saturday is yours.

how_to.counts_as_done: 40 minutes of continuous walking on Saturday.

steps.week_progression: Weeks 1-3: 40 minutes. Grows to 50 in phase 2 and 60 in phase 3.

steps.title: Check your step count at the end of the day
steps.details: Before bed, look at your phone's step count for the day. Week one is just about seeing the real number — most people are off by a thousand either way. From week two, the daily floor is 6,000.

how_to.gist: Look at today's step count before bed
how_to.why: You said you average about 4,000. Until you see the actual number each night, you're guessing — and guessing is how a 6,000-step day feels like a 9,000-step day.

sections.heading: How
sections.body: Open the health app on your phone (or whatever counts your steps) right before bed and read the day's total. That's it. No spreadsheet, no notes.

sections.heading: The floor
sections.body: Week one: just look, no target. From week two, the number you're looking for is 6,000. If it's under, a 10-minute walk around the block before bed closes the gap.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.body: The two walks are the habit; this is how you know they're working. Days you'd swear were 8,000 often turn out to be 5,000.

how_to.counts_as_done: You looked at the day's step total before bed.

steps.week_progression: Week 1: just look. Weeks 2-3: floor of 6,000 steps.

steps.title: Walk on at least 6 days this week
steps.details: One check for the whole week: did you walk on six or more days? A missed day is noise. Two missed days in a row is the thing to avoid — that's when a bad day turns into a bad week.

how_to.gist: One weekly check: did you walk on 6 or more days?
how_to.why: You're graded on the week, not on any single day. That's deliberate — it means a rained-out Tuesday doesn't end anything.

sections.heading: The rule
sections.body: Six days out of seven with at least one walk. Any walk counts — the lunch one, the after-work one, the Saturday one, or a 10-minute loop before bed.

sections.heading: If you slip
sections.body: Miss a day and nothing happens. Miss two in a row and you go out for 10 minutes that same evening, however late it is. The walk after a miss is the one that decides whether this sticks.

how_to.counts_as_done: You walked on 6 or more days this week.

steps.week_progression: Weeks 1-3: 6 walking days a week.

phases.title: Longer walks, higher floor
phases.focus: Stretch both walks and lift the daily floor as the routine starts to feel normal.

steps.title: Lunch walk
steps.details: 30 minutes now, same route extended by one block. Still starting within five minutes of finishing lunch.
steps.week_progression: Weeks 4-6: 30 minutes.

steps.title: After-work walk
steps.details: 30 minutes on arriving home, still before you sit down. Late nights stay at 15 minutes minimum.
steps.week_progression: Weeks 4-6: 30 minutes.

steps.title: Saturday long walk
steps.details: 50 minutes on Saturday, same spot you've been using. This is the walk that absorbs a rough workweek.
steps.week_progression: Weeks 4-6: 50 minutes.

steps.title: Hit 8,000 steps
steps.details: The daily floor moves to 8,000. On days the two walks don't get you there, a 10-15 minute loop before bed closes the gap.

how_to.gist: 8,000 steps today, checked before bed
how_to.why: You're two-thirds of the way to the goal. This is the number that tells you whether the two walks are actually long enough.

sections.heading: The number
sections.body: 8,000 steps by the time you go to bed. The two walks plus your normal desk-day movement should land you close — the evening loop covers the rest.

sections.heading: If you're short
sections.body: Under 8,000 at 9pm means a 10-15 minute walk around the block. It's not punishment, it's just the last 1,000 steps.

how_to.counts_as_done: The day's step total was 8,000 or more.

steps.week_progression: Weeks 4-6: 8,000 steps a day.

steps.title: Walk on at least 6 days this week
steps.details: Same weekly check as before: six or more walking days. Never two days off in a row.
steps.week_progression: Weeks 4-6: 6 walking days a week.

phases.title: Ten thousand, held
phases.focus: Reach 10,000 a day and prove you can hold it for four straight weeks.

steps.title: Lunch walk
steps.details: 30 minutes, same window, same route. This one is locked in now — it's the spine of the whole day.
steps.week_progression: Weeks 7-10: 30 minutes, unchanged.

steps.title: After-work walk
steps.details: 30 minutes on arriving home, before sitting down. Late nights: 15 minutes minimum.
steps.week_progression: Weeks 7-10: 30 minutes, unchanged.

steps.title: Saturday long walk
steps.details: 60 minutes on Saturday. This is your buffer — the day that makes the week's total safe even when work eats a weekday.
steps.week_progression: Weeks 7-10: 60 minutes.

steps.title: Hit 10,000 steps
steps.details: The goal number, every day. The two walks plus your desk-day movement should get you most of the way; a short evening loop covers the last stretch.

how_to.gist: 10,000 steps today, checked before bed
how_to.why: This is the number you came here for. Four weeks of hitting it is what turns it from a good week into your normal.

sections.heading: The number
sections.body: 10,000 steps by bedtime. Two 30-minute walks plus a normal day lands around 9,000 — the last 1,000 is a 10-minute loop after dinner.

sections.heading: If you're short
sections.body: Under 10,000 at 9pm: 10-15 minutes around the block. Do it in whatever you're already wearing.

sections.heading: The stretch
sections.body: If a day genuinely can't reach 10,000 — travel, illness, a brutal workday — the Saturday walk is what keeps the week whole.

how_to.counts_as_done: The day's step total was 10,000 or more.

steps.week_progression: Weeks 7-10: 10,000 steps a day.

steps.title: Walk on at least 6 days this week
steps.details: Six or more walking days, never two off in a row. This is the check that carries you to the finish.
steps.week_progression: Weeks 7-10: 6 walking days a week.

milestones.title: Three weeks of two walks a day
milestones.criteria: The lunch walk and the after-work walk have happened on all five workdays for three weeks running, and you've walked on at least six days each week.

milestones.title: 8,000 steps a day, held for three weeks
milestones.criteria: Your daily step count has been 8,000 or more for three straight weeks, and the Saturday walk is up to 50 minutes.

milestones.title: 10,000 steps a day, four weeks running
milestones.criteria: You've hit 10,000 steps or more every day for four consecutive weeks — the number you started at was about 4,000.

protocol.coach_notes: You're not building a walking habit from scratch — you already walk 4,000 steps a day without thinking about it. All this plan does is bolt two deliberate walks onto a day that already moves, and then slowly make them longer. The one thing that matters is the gap between the front door and the sofa: walk it before you sit down, and the rest takes care of itself. One missed day is noise. The walk you take the day after a miss is the one that decides whether this sticks.

protocol.goal_statement: Run a continuous 4k — starting from zero running, three mornings a week, built over ten weeks instead of six.

phases.title: Mostly walking, a little running
phases.focus: Get out the door three mornings and let your legs meet running in short, easy pieces.

steps.title: Monday morning walk/run
steps.details: Five minutes of brisk walking to warm up, then eight rounds of 1 minute running / 2 minutes walking, then walk the last few minutes home. The running minutes should feel like you could hold a conversation — if you're gasping, slow down.

how_to.gist: 25 minutes: brisk walk, then 8 rounds of 1 min run / 2 min walk
how_to.why: Your legs and lungs need to meet running in small doses first. Short running pieces with walking between them build the base without wrecking your shins in week two.

sections.heading: The session
items: 5 min brisk walk to start
8 rounds: 1 min run, 2 min walk
Walk the last few minutes home

sections.heading: The pace
sections.body: The running minutes should be slow enough that you could talk in short sentences. If you're gasping, you're going too fast — this is about time on your feet, not speed.

sections.heading: If it feels hard
sections.body: Cut the running minutes to 45 seconds and keep the walking at 2 minutes. Finishing the session matters more than the exact numbers.

how_to.counts_as_done: 25 minutes done, walking included

steps.week_progression: Weeks 1-3 hold this shape; the running pieces get slightly longer each week.

steps.title: Wednesday morning walk/run
steps.details: Same as Monday: 5 minutes brisk walking, then eight rounds of 1 minute running / 2 minutes walking, then walk home. A day of walking in between is what keeps this from turning into a shin problem.

how_to.gist: Repeat Monday's session — 8 rounds of 1 min run / 2 min walk
how_to.why: Three mornings a week with a rest day between each is the dose your legs can absorb. Running on back-to-back days is the fastest way to end up sore and stopped.

sections.heading: The session
items: 5 min brisk walk to start
8 rounds: 1 min run, 2 min walk
Walk the last few minutes home

sections.heading: The rule
sections.body: Never two running mornings in a row. Monday, Wednesday, Friday — the gaps are part of the training, not time off from it.

how_to.counts_as_done: 25 minutes done, walking included

steps.week_progression: Same shape as Monday, running pieces lengthening week by week.

steps.title: Friday morning walk/run
steps.details: The third session of the week, same structure: brisk walk to start, eight rounds of 1 minute running / 2 minutes walking, walk home. If the week has gone badly, this is the one to keep — three out of three is what builds the habit.

how_to.gist: Third session of the week — same 8 rounds of 1 min run / 2 min walk
how_to.why: Three mornings a week is what you told me you can give, and it's exactly the dose this build needs. Friday closes the week and sets up two days of rest.

sections.heading: The session
items: 5 min brisk walk to start
8 rounds: 1 min run, 2 min walk
Walk the last few minutes home

sections.heading: If you miss one
sections.body: One missed morning is noise. The one that matters is the next one — get out the door on the following scheduled day and the week still counts.

how_to.counts_as_done: 25 minutes done, walking included

steps.week_progression: Same shape; running pieces grow across weeks 1-3.

steps.title: Kit by the door the night before
steps.details: The night before each running morning, put your trainers, socks and a filled water bottle by the front door and set your alarm. Nothing to find, nothing to decide at 6am.

how_to.gist: Night before: trainers, socks and water by the door, alarm set
how_to.why: The mornings you skip are the ones where you had to hunt for something. Removing that step is the whole trick — the decision is already made when you wake up.

sections.heading: What goes out
items: Trainers
Socks
Filled water bottle
Alarm set for the morning

sections.heading: When
sections.body: Do it right before bed on Sunday, Tuesday and Thursday nights, so it's waiting for Monday, Wednesday and Friday mornings.

how_to.counts_as_done: Kit is by the door and the alarm is set before you go to bed

steps.week_progression: Keep this going all ten weeks — it's the cheapest thing in the plan.

phases.title: Running gets longer, walking gets shorter
phases.focus: Stretch the running pieces and shrink the walking breaks while keeping every session easy.

steps.title: Monday morning run/walk
steps.details: Five minutes brisk walking, then six rounds of 3 minutes running / 2 minutes walking, then walk home. Still conversational — you should be able to say a sentence while running.

how_to.gist: 30 minutes: 6 rounds of 3 min run / 2 min walk
how_to.why: The running pieces are getting long enough to build real endurance now. The walking breaks are still there so you never have to stop early.

how_to.gist: Repeat Monday's session — 6 rounds of 3 min run / 2 min walk
how_to.why: Two days between sessions is what lets your legs recover. Wednesday is the session people push too hard — keep it as easy as Monday.

how_to.gist: Third session — 6 rounds of 3 min run / 2 min walk

steps.title: Easy week every fourth week
steps.details: Every fourth week, cut the running pieces back to what you did two weeks earlier and keep the walking breaks generous. Weeks 4 and 8 are the easy ones here — you'll feel like you're going backwards, and that's the point.

how_to.gist: Every 4th week, drop back to the previous week's easier session
how_to.why: Tendons and joints catch up during easier weeks, not during hard ones. Skipping the step-back is how people get to week seven with sore shins and stop.

sections.heading: What changes
sections.body: Run the session from two weeks earlier — shorter running pieces, longer walking breaks. Same three mornings, same time out the door.

sections.heading: Why it's here
sections.body: Your heart and lungs adapt faster than your legs do. The easy week is when the legs catch up.

phases.title: Long running blocks, short walks
phases.focus: Run in long stretches with brief walking breaks, and get used to being out for a full 4k.

steps.title: Monday morning long blocks
steps.details: Five minutes brisk walking, then three rounds of 8 minutes running / 1 minute walking, then walk home. The walking minutes are a reset, not a rest — keep moving through them.

how_to.gist: 35 minutes: 3 rounds of 8 min run / 1 min walk
how_to.why: Eight-minute running blocks are close to what a continuous 4k asks of you. The one-minute walks keep you honest about pace.

sections.body: Slow enough to talk. If the last block feels like a fight, the first one was too fast.

sections.heading: If it feels hard
sections.body: Go back to 5 minutes running / 2 minutes walking for this week. Better to repeat a week than to limp through one.

how_to.why: You're two weeks from the 4k. Backing off now means arriving at it with fresh legs instead of a sore shin.

phases.title: The continuous 4k
phases.focus: Take the walking breaks out and run the whole 4k without stopping.

steps.title: Monday morning continuous run
steps.details: Five minutes brisk walking, then run continuously for 20 minutes without stopping, then walk home. Slow is the whole game — this should feel easier than the long-block sessions did.

how_to.gist: 20 minutes running with no walking breaks, then walk home
how_to.why: This is the first time you'll run without stopping. Twenty minutes at an easy pace is most of the way to a 4k.

sections.heading: The pace
sections.body: Start slower than feels right. The mistake here is going out at the pace you ran the short blocks — you'll be walking by minute twelve.

sections.heading: If you have to walk
sections.body: Walk for a minute, then start running again. A 20-minute run with one walking minute in it still counts as the session.

how_to.gist: Repeat Monday — 20 minutes continuous, then walk home
how_to.why: Doing it twice in a week is what turns a one-off into something you can rely on.

steps.title: Run the full 4k
steps.details: In week 10, one of your three mornings is the whole thing: 4k, running the entire way, no walking breaks. Warm up with five minutes of brisk walking, then go. Pick the morning you feel best — Monday or Friday usually beats Wednesday.

how_to.gist: Run the full 4k without stopping, once in week 10
how_to.why: This is the goal you came in with, ten weeks of mornings behind it. You've run every piece of this distance already — just never all at once.

sections.heading: The pace
sections.body: Start slower than you think you need to. The first kilometre should feel almost too easy — that's what leaves you something for the last one.

sections.heading: If you have to walk
sections.body: Walk, then run again. If it happens, repeat week 10 and run it clean the following week — the distance is already yours.

protocol.coach_notes: Ten weeks instead of six isn't a softer goal — it's the same 4k with a runway your legs can actually use. The mornings you'll want to skip are the ones that matter most, and the rule is simple: one missed morning is nothing, two in a row is how this plan dies. Get out the door on the next scheduled day and you're still on track.
